strategies.summary: With a higher-timeframe opposing draw on liquidity in view, fade the opening Judas swing when price trades into the first line of defense or sweeps the last line of defense. The first line is usually a fair value gap and the last line is the opposing swing extreme.

timeframes.notes: 4h or daily context defines the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity; 15m marks the FLOT/LOT area; entries are refined on 1m or 5m. Written on the canonical bullish side; bearish examples are mirror cases.

glossary.FLOT: First line of defense: the first retracement PD array, usually a fair value gap; see custom_signals.flod.
glossary.LOT: Last line of defense: the opposing swing extreme that must hold after the manipulation; see custom_signals.llod.

custom_signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.

custom_signals.name: london_open_price
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opening price at 02:00 New York time (start of the London kill zone).

custom_signals.name: midnight_open
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opening price at 00:00 New York time of the current NY day.

custom_signals.name: weekly_open
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opening price at Monday 00:00 New York time of the current week.

custom_signals.name: judas_swing
custom_signals.plain_definition: The manipulation leg: an initial fake move away from the opening price, opposite to the real move, before the expansion.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: lowest(low, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 1) < custom_signals.midnight_open AND close > custom_signals.midnight_open

custom_signals.name: flod
custom_signals.plain_definition: First line of defense: the first PD array met on a retracement, most often a fair value gap.

custom_signals.name: llod
custom_signals.plain_definition: Last line of defense: the swing extreme at the origin of the current price leg.

custom_signals.name: opening_judas_swing
custom_signals.plain_definition: A counter-trend manipulation leg trades below the London session open, below the New York midnight open during the New York AM session, or below the Monday open, then closes back above that opening price.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (kill_zone == london AND ny_minute >= 02:00 AND lowest(low, ((ny_minute - 02:00) / tf_minutes) + 1) < custom_signals.london_open_price AND close > custom_signals.london_open_price) OR (kill_zone == new_york_am AND custom_signals.judas_swing) OR (lowest(low, (((ny_dow - 1) * 1440 + ny_minute) / tf_minutes) + 1) < custom_signals.weekly_open AND close > custom_signals.weekly_open)

custom_signals.name: judas_reversal_zone_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: An opening Judas swing reaches the first line of defense, usually a bullish fair value gap, or sweeps the last line of defense and closes back above it.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.opening_judas_swing AND ((custom_signals.flod AND low <= custom_signals.flod AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) OR (low <= custom_signals.llod AND close >= custom_signals.llod))

sequence: With an opposing higher-timeframe draw on liquidity already marked, fade the opening Judas swing when it taps the first line of defense or sweeps the last line of defense and reclaims it.

invalidation.text: If there is a fair value gap in the leg (FLOT), price should respect it and likely not sweep the LOT.
The Judas swing should not come back below the LOT.

filters.text: Do not expect the Judas swing to sweep an unreasonable amount of liquidity outside the average daily volatility.
Be cautious on days with no economic calendar news events (like some Mondays), as price might lack the energy to expand.

entry_rule.text: For the bullish reading, buy the retracement as the opening Judas swing trades into the first line of defense or briefly sweeps the last line of defense.
entry_rule.quote: when you have that retracement you want to get involved here to ride that expansion

target_rule.text: Target the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity, typically the first opposing premium array or swing objective above price.
target_rule.quote: what is the first discount array that we cannot reach for it it is this swing low

stop_rule.text: For the bullish reading, place the stop beyond the last line of defense.
stop_rule.quote: it shouldn't come back below this low it should not sweep this low

presenter_claims.claim: If you know where price is likely going higher from, you can make millions.

strategies.notes: The higher-timeframe draw on liquidity is the presenter's context, not the engine's BOS/CHoCH bias. The machine setup uses the registry's London, daily-midnight and Monday-open anchors; the missing ES example's equities-open variant is therefore not separately encoded here. FLOT uses a touch into the fair value gap, not the engine's CE-based fvg.mitigated event.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: The New York session begins, initiating a counter-trend Judas Swing.
The fake move trades directly into the First Line of Defense (FLOT), which is a Fair Value Gap.
Price respects the FLOT FVG without sweeping the Last Line of Defense (LOT) and subsequently expands in the true direction.

examples.presenter_commentary: He introduces the FLOT (First Line of Defense) and LOT (Last Line of Defense) concepts here. He stresses that when an FVG exists in the leg (FLOT), the Judas swing should mitigate it and protect the extreme LOT.

may_differ.reason: The presenter treats any trade into the FLOT fair value gap as sufficient, while the engine marks fvg.mitigated only when price reaches the CE midpoint.
Presenter uses generic session-open timing rather than only Traidle's fixed kill-zone windows.
